Both translations are correct and natural. A few notes:

- **"Commencez votre essai gratuit"**: Correct. This is the standard imperative (vous form) for a CTA. "Démarrez votre essai gratuit" and "Essayez gratuitement" are common alternatives, and the latter is shorter for buttons.
- **"Pas de carte de crédit nécessaire"**: Grammatical and understandable, but a bit literal. More idiomatic options:
  - **"Aucune carte bancaire requise"** is the most common phrasing on French signup pages. French speakers say "carte bancaire" (or "carte bleue" colloquially) far more often than "carte de crédit," which sounds Canadian or like an anglicism in France.
  - **"Sans carte bancaire"** is shorter and works well under a button.

If your audience is in Québec, "carte de crédit" is the normal term there, so your version works. In that case "Aucune carte de crédit requise" is slightly more polished.

Also, make sure you use the same register (vous vs. tu) across the rest of the page. Your first line uses vous, so keep that consistent.
